blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask: When Recurrent ‘Hemorrhagic’ Effusions Are Pancreatic
blogs.description: A practical approach to the patient with recurrent, dark red unilateral pleural effusions—including the red flags that should trigger a search for a pancreatopleural fistula (PPF). Covers why respiratory symptoms dominate while the pathology is abdominal, what elements of history (e.g., recent blunt abdominal trauma) to re-ask, and how early pleural fluid amylase testing can avert misdiagnosis and repeated thoracenteses.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase 101: Ordering, Interpreting, and Avoiding TB Traps
blogs.description: When and how to check pleural amylase; thresholds suggestive of PPF (often >1,000 IU/L); interpreting pancreatic vs salivary isoenzymes; and distinguishing PPF from esophageal perforation and malignancy. Explores pitfalls of leaning on mildly elevated ADA and TB contact in endemic regions, with a stepwise lab strategy to prevent inappropriate anti-tubercular therapy.

blogs.title: Handlebar to Hemithorax: Blunt Abdominal Trauma as a Hidden Cause of PPF in Kids
blogs.description: Mechanisms by which pancreatic duct disruption or pseudocyst can track via the esophageal hiatus to the pleural space, often after seemingly minor bicycle-handlebar injury. Highlights delayed presentations, patient under-reporting, and the right-sided or even bilateral effusions that can follow—plus the value of a second-pass trauma history in pediatric dyspnea.

blogs.title: Imaging the Invisible Leak: CT, MRCP, or ERCP for Suspected PPF?
blogs.description: A comparative, pragmatic imaging playbook: what CT reliably shows (pancreatic collections, hydropneumothorax) vs its limited fistula visualization; MRCP’s ~70–80% sensitivity and ductal mapping without radiation; and ERCP’s role as the gold standard for therapeutic planning. Includes what to look for on each modality and how to sequence studies in a deteriorating child.

blogs.title: Closing the Leak: A Management Pathway for Pediatric Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: A bedside algorithm from ED to ward/PICU: NPO, TPN, somatostatin analogs (octreotide 10–40 mcg/kg/day), pancreatic enzyme replacement, and controlled thoracic drainage. Reviews reported pediatric success rates (conservative ~12%), when to escalate to ERCP with transpapillary stenting (closure often within 2–3 weeks; high success in small pediatric series), and surgical options with outcomes when endoscopy fails.

blogs.title: Right-Sided Hydropneumothorax in a Child? Think Retroperitoneum-to-Hiatus Fistula
blogs.description: Why PPFs can preferentially present on the right and even be bilateral, and how air-fluid levels can misdirect toward empyema. Reviews anatomic routes (aortic/esophageal hiatus), clues on CXR/CT, and chest tube pearls (drain for relief but keep searching for the abdominal source).

blogs.title: The Recurrent Effusion That Wasn’t TB: Diagnostic Bias in Endemic Settings
blogs.description: A cognitive debrief on anchoring bias when ADA is modestly elevated and there’s TB contact. Outlines a rational test order (amylase, cytology, GeneXpert, pH, triglycerides) and a checklist to avoid premature anti-TB therapy when the effusion is large, recurrent, hemorrhagic, afebrile, and amylase-rich.

blogs.title: Beyond the Effusion: Genetics and the Pediatric Pancreas
blogs.description: When a child presents with pancreatitis or PPF, consider underlying PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR, or CTRC variants—especially with recurrence or a family history. Offers a brief approach to who merits genetic evaluation, how results influence counseling and recurrence risk, and why trauma can unmask a predisposed pancreas.
